reason: Conversation 1 correctly identified H98 as the HV inverter/no-microwave-output fault, gave the right safety boundary (no opening the case, lethal stored voltages) and escalated to Panasonic or an engineer in one turn, though it assumed rather than clarified that H98 was a display code and skipped a power reset. Conversation 2 never engaged with the H98 code even after the customer supplied it and the full model, instead misdiagnosing an overheat cut-out, asking irrelevant questions about power level and vents, repeatedly calling the appliance a 'Panasonic NNH98' (treating the code as a model), and gave no honest answer on repair-vs-replace when asked. Both stayed safe, but 1 was correct and efficient while 2 was wrong and wasted the homeowner's time.
